siblingApproaches.approach: From the Stuart Lake/Colchuck Lake Trailhead (~3,500 ft, end of Eightmile Road/FR-7601), follow the Stuart Lake Trail (#1599) about 2.5 miles to the signed fork where the Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599.1) splits left/south. Continue roughly 1.8 more miles — crossing Mountaineer Creek and a boulder-hop stretch near the outlet — to Colchuck Lake (5,570 ft, ~4.3 mi in), the last easy, reliable water before the pass. siblingApproaches.approach: Begins on Chair Peak's north ridge, reached via the East Face/Northeast Buttress approach (Alpental parking, Snow Lake Trail, Source Lake fork, then a gully to roughly 4,800 ft and the basin below), then continues along the crest over/past Bryant Peak.

From the Alpental parking lot, take the Snow Lake Trail; at about 1.5 miles turn off toward Source Lake. Ascend a 3rd-class rocky gully starting around 4,200 ft, reach a small cliff around 4,800 ft, traverse through a notch, then cross a snowy basin to the base of the route around 5,500 ft.

siblingApproaches.approach: Hike the Stuart Lake Trail (#1599) and the Colchuck Lake Trail (#1599.1) from the Stuart Lake Trailhead (FS Road 7601 off Icicle Creek Road) — 4 miles and 2,280 ft gain, crossing Mountaineer Creek on a log bridge at 1.5 miles and staying left at the Lake Stuart Trail junction — to reach Colchuck Lake (2.5-3 hours). siblingTrailheads.trailheadDirection: From Darrington, drive Highway 530 to the Suiattle River Road (Forest Road 26) and turn east; the trailhead is in a parking lot just past the Downey Creek bridge, about 20 miles from Highway 530. siblingApproaches.approach: The standard approach is from the Downey Creek Trailhead (off Suiattle River Road) via the southern end of the Ptarmigan Traverse — a rugged, largely off-trail alpine route over Itswoot Ridge/Cub Lake and Bachelor Creek involving glacier travel and significant bushwhacking. Climbers typically budget a full day (or two) of approach before reaching the base of North Peak's granite West Face; this is an experienced-mountaineers-only objective, not a roadside crag.

siblingApproaches.approach: From the Snowgrass Flats Trailhead (end of FR-2150, elev. ~4,600 ft), start on Trail 96 (Snowgrass Flat Trail).
